title: Cron scheduled tasks for multi-instance apps
description: Run cron jobs from a server app with several instances: five-field cron with names and macros, next runs in any IANA time zone with defined DST behavior, one execution per occurrence across instances, skip/queue/allow overlap policies with leases and heartbeats, catch-up policies for downtime, retries with backoff, an onFailure hook, run history and a PostgreSQL store.

notes: Requires a TypeScript build, Intl.DateTimeFormat with IANA time-zone data (full ICU), AbortController, structuredClone and crypto.randomUUID: Node.js 22+, Bun, Deno and Cloudflare Workers.
Framework-neutral core; call tick() from your own loop, platform cron route or worker every few seconds to a minute.
No runtime packages, environment reads, timers or network activity at install or import time; the optional heartbeat timer exists only while a handler runs.

configuration: On PostgreSQL, apply schema.sql and use createSqlSchedulerStore with your query executor; on other databases implement SchedulerStore with a unique (schedule_id, scheduled_for) key and single-statement conditional updates for materialize, claim, slot, heartbeat and finish, and a due-run query that returns at most one run per schedule.
Register handlers by name in createScheduler({handlers}); saved schedules store only the name and JSON payload, never code.
Give each process a unique instanceId and call tick() at least once per graceMs (default 60 s); a platform cron route that hits one instance per minute also works.

Pick per schedule: timeZone (IANA, default UTC), overlap (skip, queue or allow), catchUp (none, latest or all with maxCatchUp), maxAttempts and retry delays, and a leaseMs above your handler's longest pause between heartbeats.
Make handlers idempotent per (scheduleId, scheduledFor): a run whose worker crashes after committing effects is retried after its lease expires.
Pass onFailure to alert when a run fails for good, and prune old rows from scheduled_task_runs on a schedule.
limitations: Execution is at least once: a worker that crashes after its handler committed effects but before the run was marked finished has the run retried after the lease expires. Handlers must be idempotent per occurrence.

Supports five-field cron only: no seconds field, ?, L, W, # or @reboot. Schedules match wall-clock minutes, so a frequent schedule (for example */5) runs once per wall time and pauses during the repeated hour of a fall-back transition; use timeZone UTC for interval-style jobs.
The time-zone conversion assumes at most one offset change within 26 hours, which holds for current tz data. Results depend on the runtime's ICU time-zone data version.
The automatic heartbeat keeps a hung handler's lease alive indefinitely; there is no handler timeout. Watch the signal and enforce your own deadlines.
Under overlap queue a pending retry can run after a newer occurrence; skip records skipped occurrences in run history but does not alert.

The in-memory store is for tests and single-process prototypes. The SQL store is tested on PostgreSQL semantics through PGlite, which runs one connection, so contention across separate connections is not exercised there.
Production database correctness, tick hosting, handler idempotency and consuming-application acceptance remain project responsibilities.
decisions: 5-field cron only (no seconds, L, W, #); a DST-skipped time runs once after the gap
payload max 64 KiB; handlers by name; no HTTP routes, drive tick() from your own timer or cron
options: timeZone (default UTC); overlap skip|queue|allow (skip); catchUp none|latest|all (latest), maxCatchUp
maxAttempts (3); retryBaseMs, retryMaxMs: doubling delay (30 s to 1 h); leaseMs, graceMs (60 s)

verification.command: npm run build && node --test tests/scheduled-tasks.test.mjs tests/scheduled-tasks-sql.test.mjs
behaviors: parseCron accepts ranges, steps, lists, month and weekday names, Sunday as 0 or 7 and @macros, and rejects malformed fields, seconds, ?, L, W, # and @reboot
save rejects invalid cron, unknown time zones, unregistered handlers, bad options, non-JSON payloads or payloads over 64 KiB of UTF-8 and expressions that never match (0 0 30 2 *)
next runs follow the Vixie day-of-month OR day-of-week rule and leap days, including 2096 to 2104
America/New_York: a time in the spring-forward gap runs once at the end of the gap; a time repeated by fall-back runs once, at its first occurrence
three or four concurrent instances on one memory store and on PGlite run each occurrence exactly once; concurrent materializations of one occurrence insert one row
overlap skip records a skipped occurrence, queue defers it until the running occurrence finishes, allow runs both
due-run queries return one run per schedule, so a queue schedule with a backlog of more than 100 rows does not starve other schedules (memory store and PGlite)
the minimum lease is 3000 ms; with the automatic heartbeat every leaseMs/3, a handler lasting four leases executes once while another instance ticks
heartbeats extend the lease; after a crashed worker's lease expires another instance reclaims the run and the slot, and the stale worker's result is discarded
catchUp none skips missed occurrences, latest runs the most recent, all runs the most recent maxCatchUp oldest first; a month-long gap stays bounded
failed runs retry with exponential backoff up to maxAttempts, then fail with a truncated error and call onFailure once; a crash in the final attempt fails without re-running
schema.sql applies and the SQL store passes the core behaviors on PostgreSQL

changes: First release: time-zone aware cron engine, scheduler core with overlap, catch-up and retry policies, in-memory store, PostgreSQL schema and store.
